name: Ibn ʿAqīl
known: Bahāʾ al-Dīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān
summary: Cairene grammarian whose commentary on the Alfiyya is the one most students read with Ibn Mālik's poem.
bio: Ibn ʿAqīl was born in Cairo around 694/1294 and died there in 769/1367. Not much is known of his life; he wrote on Shāfiʿī law as well as on grammar.
His Sharḥ on the Alfiyya explains each verse plainly with examples, and with the Alfiyya it became a standard text of the traditional curriculum.
